name: JS heap size
plain: Chromium reports JavaScript heap size limits, which track device RAM.
meaning: jsHeapSizeLimit is about 2 to 4 GB on 64-bit desktops and 0.5 to 1 GB on low-end phones, bucketed in Chrome, so it hints at RAM class even though deviceMemory is capped at 8.

access.persistence: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored
access.iframe: Readable from cross-origin iframes too (same values)

limits.headline: Can see how much memory the page can use, which hints at your RAM class
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens when the page runs in Chrome or Edge
can: Check the JavaScript memory limit and how much is used
Guess a low, mid, or high RAM device from the limit
Tune how much the page loads at once
Use it as a hardware clue
cannot: Work in Firefox, Safari, or on iPhone
See memory used by other tabs or apps
See precise numbers; Chrome rounds them into buckets
limits.reach_label: A rough memory class, in Chrome
limits.differs: Only Chromium browsers share it. Firefox and Safari do not.

story.what_it_is: Chrome tells a page how much working memory its JavaScript is allowed to use, which hints at your device's RAM.
story.for_you: You never see it. It is one of the numbers a page can read that quietly shows whether you have a small or large machine, even when other memory numbers are hidden.
story.for_makers: Developers use it to find memory leaks and to learn when a tab is close to crashing. Fingerprinting code uses the same limit to guess RAM class. Chrome rounds the numbers, so the hint is rough.

use_cases.example: A web app team logs heap size in tests to find a leak that slowly eats memory.
A large browser game checks the heap limit and loads smaller maps on devices with a low limit.
A browser design tool warns before opening a huge file that would exceed the tab's memory.
A big spreadsheet in the browser avoids loading everything at once when memory is tight.
A bot detector notes that a headless browser reports a typical server heap size and flags it.
An ad tech script uses heap size to guess a device tier for choosing heavier or lighter ads.

history.change: Values bucketed and jittered to reduce precision
